articles.title: Broadcasters and governing bodies make tax plea for TV coverage of women’s sport
articles.summary: Letter sent to chancellor, John Healey, on Friday. ‘Audience demand for women’s sport is growing’ The chief executives of the Football Association, Rugby Football Union and England and Wales Cricket Board have joined forces with leading broadcasters and YouTube in writing to the chancellor…
body: In a letter signed by 25 representatives of the country’s biggest sports and broadcasters, including Sky Sports and ITV, the government is urged to extend to women’s sport production the audio-visual expenditure credit scheme that provides tax relief to independent films and children’s television.

The joint letter, was sent to John Healey on Friday to coincide with this weekend’s return of the Women’s Super League, whose chief executive, Nikki Doucet, is among the signatories, along with the bosses of British Cycling, golf and Formula One.
The WSL is the second-richest league in women’s sport after National Women’s Soccer League in the US, but faces challenges attracting broadcasters in a congested market.

Every WSL fixture will be broadcast live in the UK this season, with WSL2 games available on YouTube, but the BBC has taken the controversial decision to axe its weekly highlights programme, The Women’s Football Show.

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen and Sindarov to meet at least twice in IPL-styled Global Chess League
articles.summary: Fans would have preferred contest for world crown, but 20-minute Rapid games are still competitive substitute. Magnus Carlsen, the world No 1, will be paired at least twice in the next few days with the world championship challenger, Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov, in the Tech Mahindra Global Chess…
body: In 2024 the Global League was staged in London, but this year it is back in India at Bengaluru (formerly Bangalore), India’s technology capital, from 5-13 September, finishing two days before the 400-team chess Olympiad opens in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

Carlsen will play on the top or icon board for the defending champions, Alpine APL Pipers, as will Sindarov for Fyers American Gambits. Other icons are Alireza Firouzja (Triveni Continental Kings), Ian Nepomniachtchi (Ganges Grandmasters), former world champion Viswanathan Anand (PBG Alaskan Knights) and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave (CheQ Mumba Masters). The supporting male players include Turkey’s fast rising record breaker Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, 15, while the women stars are led by the Candidates runner-up, Bibisara Assaubayeva.

Carlsen and Sindarov will play two games, one with each colour, in the preliminary all-play-all, with a third and perhaps a fourth to follow if both their teams reach the semi-finals, third-place match, or final stages. The time limit will be 20 minutes for the entire game, plus a two seconds per move increment from move 41.

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr once turned boxing upside down. Can he do it again at 36?
articles.summary: Seven years after springing one of the biggest upsets in boxing history, the Mexican Rocky is back with his old trainer for one final run at the heavyweight summit. Seven years ago, Andy Ruiz Jr became the first fighter of Mexican descent to win the world heavyweight championship in one of the…
body: A replacement opponent summoned on five weeks’ notice who went off as an 11-1 underdog, Ruiz came off the canvas in the third to knock Joshua down four times before the referee finally waved it off. Hailed as the “Mexican Rocky”, he was lionized as a border-straddling hero in his hometown of Imperial, the dusty agricultural community framed by the mountain ranges and flat deserts of south-eastern California. He made the late-night rounds, took an audience with Mexico president Andrés Manuel López Obrador and signed a $10m guarantee when Joshua activated his rematch clause. The money, cars, fame and women arrived all at once.

articles.title: Tough start for PSG but Luis Enrique has faith in burst of ‘new energy’ from signings
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain have drawn both of their league games so far Monaco pose a tricky task on Friday. “It’s like we’re at school,” Luis Enrique quipped as he entered the press conference room, hearing the journalists respond in unison to his hearty bonjour.
body: His remark was fitting on the eve of Paris Saint-Germain’s first home match of the season, which lines up nicely with France’s rentrée, the term for the nationwide return to school and the office at the start of September. Although the new campaign is in full swing by now, the team have had to wait several weeks before making their return to the Parc des Princes, where they welcome second place Monaco on Friday night.

The league champions were due to start the season by hosting Rennes on the first day, but successive heatwaves over the summer had damaged the Parc des Princes pitch to the extent that the match was instead moved to Brittany. Rennes were also hoping to host the return match in March as scheduled, but the league authorities instead switched the two fixtures around in the calendar.

This year’s rentrée has not exactly seen a swift return to business as usual for the perennial Ligue 1 champions. Since beating Aston Villa to retain the Uefa Super Cup last month, PSG have lost the Trophée des Champions to Lens and drawn their first two league matches.

articles.title: 100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette'
articles.summary: The behaviour of influencers and content creators has become a major talking point at this year's US Open amid incidents of matches being disrupted.
body: When it comes to etiquette in tennis, there are a fair few unwritten rules.
Apologising after winning a point from a net cord. Honesty around line calls, double bounces and double-hits. Post-match handshakes.
As for the spectators, it is common courtesy not to disturb the players during points.
Around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for the tournament in New York - double the amount from last year.

articles.summary: An inside look at Katie Taylor's emotional final fight week as 80,000 fans prepare to salute Ireland's boxing icon at Croke Park on Saturday.
body: Katie Taylor smiles as she sits down for her fight-week media commitments, but her eyes give her away.

On Saturday, she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili at Croke Park, bringing down the curtain on a career that has gone from disguising herself as a boy in a sport that barred women, to Olympic gold and undisputed titles.
The weight of a lifetime in the ring is catching up with an Irish icon preparing to step away.
"I thought I was handling all the emotions until today," the 40-year-old tells BBC Sport.

articles.title: Real Madrid reserve two roles for club icon Luka Modric after retirement – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid already has two potential paths in mind for Luka Modric once the club legend eventually ends his playing career, according to Defensa Central. Modric continues to perform at AC Milan, but the question of what comes next has already started to emerge.
body: The Croatian midfielder recently said in an interview with AS that he would like to return to Madrid one day, although only if he can make a meaningful contribution rather than simply come back because of his status as a club icon.
Now, Journalist Tomas Roncero, as relayed in Defensa Central, believes that a return is inevitable.
More importantly, he thinks Modric has the football knowledge to take on a serious role at the club rather than becoming a ceremonial figure.
“I noticed that he will definitely return to Madrid and I am convinced that he doesn’t want to return to Madrid as an ambassador, but rather he wants to feel important,” Roncero explained.

articles.title: From playing with Rashford to non-league and new career
articles.summary: Ten years after lining up with Marcus Rashford for Manchester United, Joe Riley tells BBC Sport about his new career - and why he does not miss full-time football.
body: A Tuesday night in Workington in late August and Joe Riley leads his Warrington Rylands team-mates out for a match at the Fibrus Community Stadium in the seventh tier of English football.
Rylands race into a 2-0 lead in Cumbria before losing 3-2 after having two players sent off in a chaotic Northern Premier League Premier Division encounter played in front of 638 supporters.
"A few years back I wouldn't speak for 24 hours if I lost," says Riley, whose side host Hyde United in the first qualifying round of the FA Cup on Saturday (15:00 BST).
"Now if we lose, it's not ideal, but there's always another game around the corner."

articles.title: Pol Espargaro to replace Maverick Vinales again at Tech3 KTM
articles.summary: After competing in the British and Aragon grands prix, Pol Espargaro will contest next week's San Marino Grand Prix with Tech3 KTM, replacing Maverick Vinales. Vinales continues to recover from the injury he suffered last year to his left shoulder, in a qualifying crash at the Sachsenring.
body: Vinales had to miss several races early in 2026 and eventually underwent surgery on 1 April to have a screw removed from the affected area which supposedly was the cause of his problems.
Despite the operation, the Spaniard has failed to and, since returning at Barcelona in mid-May, his performances and results have never been close to expectations.

It was expected that Vinales could return in form after the summer break, but he has been kept away from the track by his physical problems and the KTM/Tech3 conflict over his contract. Last month, Motorsport.com revealed KTM intended to drop Vinales altogether for the remainder of the season.

"While our priority remains supporting Maverick in his recovery, we are pleased to have Pol back with us in Misano," explained Tech3 director Nicolas Goyon. "Pol knows the team very well and has already demonstrated his professionalism and commitment in his two latest appearances this season. Returning to MotoGP is never easy, but Pol brings valuable experience and we are looking forward to working with him again in San Marino. We wish Maverick a more satisfactory recovery and hope to see him again when he is ready."

articles.title: What Paige Bueckers thinks of playing with Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston on Team USA
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers gets candid about sharing the court with two Indiana Fever stars. Dallas Wings star Paige Bueckers has been called up to represent Team USA at the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup.
body: It’s a phenomenal opportunity for the young guard, as her talent will be on display for the entire world. It will also give fans a peek at how well she gels with their WNBA rivals.

Previously, Bueckers had been very vocal about playing with Angel Reese on Team USA. Now, ahead of the opening game of the tournament against Team China, Paige shared her honest thoughts on being on the court with Indiana Fever stars Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston.
“Honestly, we have great on-court chemistry. It’s kind of natural and organic. It’s been a while since we played together, but it’s almost like no time has passed.
“With Caitlin, you want to run the floor, be a great wing, be a great cutter, move off the ball,” Bueckers said of Clark.

articles.title: Andrews: Brentford are playing with verve - let's see if we can break the ceiling
articles.summary: Seconds before the curtain came down on the 2025/26 season, Brentford had a golden chance to do what they had never done before: qualify for Europe.
body: They were drawing 1-1 with Liverpool at Anfield and knew that one goal would be enough to finish seventh and secure Europa League football.

In the 10th minute of added time, Mikkel Damsgaard dropped the ball off to Vitaly Janelt on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The midfielder hit a cross first time that curled in the most inviting way to the centre of the box.
Kevin Schade was waiting for it, but Dango Ouattara got there first - and steered it off target.
Keith Andrews put his head in his hands and sank to his knees. His first season as a head coach had nearly ended in the most perfect way.

articles.title: 😲 Surprise move: Bundesliga club leaves captain out of CL squad!
articles.summary: Next week is the moment: the 2026/27 Champions League season kicks off on Tuesday! Over the past few hours, many clubs have gradually announced their squads for Europe’s premier competition.
body: Important: Each team may register a maximum of 25 players on the so-called “A list.” In addition, certain rules must be met, especially regarding the inclusion of homegrown youth players.

Even more important: the squads are not final. After the end of the league phase in January, Champions League participants are allowed to make changes to their squad once again. For now, however, the teams are set.

That, in turn, is bad news for Emre Can. The regular BVB captain has been dealing with a torn ACL since March, but according to recent media reports, he is expected to make his comeback during the first half of the season.

At least in the Champions League, however, that will not happen. The Germany international will only be an option there from the knockout stage onward. So from Can’s point of view, all that remains is to hope that his teammates do not do anything foolish and, as expected, qualify for the playoffs—or even directly for the round of 16.

articles.title: Kyrgios accepts one-month suspension after positive cocaine test
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios has accepted ‌and served a reduced, one-month suspension under anti-doping rules after testing positive ‌for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in ​Mallorca.
body: Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules.
The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.
The drug is banned in competition and the former Wimbledon finalist has been provisionally suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play or attend tournaments.

During an ​interview with ITIA investigators, the 31-year-old ⁠explained that his use ⁠of cocaine had "occurred socially" during a night out before he was due ‌to play in Mallorca, the statement said.

articles.title: Inside the neighbourhood club that made Arteta, Alonso and Iraola
articles.summary: Between a row of white apartment buildings and an artificial pitch set into the green hills of Berio in San Sebastian that Antiguoko now call home, there is a strip of land where Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola learned their craft.
body: "The centre circle was just over there," says Roberto Montiel, the club's long-serving coach and vice-president, as he takes a seat in what is now a public park. He rubs his thumb and forefinger together as he recalls the texture of the old playing surface.

"The pitch wasn't like the new one up there. It was smaller and made of small stones, like gravel. The balls weren't like the ones now either. When they got wet, they became heavy. You would slip and slide, and if you fell, you'd end up with a terrible scrape."
The games played here by this neighbourhood club's celebrated alumni, two of whom meet as managers when Arsenal face Chelsea on Sky Sports on Sunday, are the stuff of local legend.
"Even then you could see their vision for the game," adds Montiel.
